newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian energy firms seek secure state payments.
newsitem.headline: Russian energy firms seek secure state payments.

text.p: Russia's largest gas and electricity suppliers, dogged by non-payments from government bodies, want separate budget allocations for energy payments in next year's budget to stop new debts building up.
In return they are prepared to restructure existing debts over seven to 10 years, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kirikenko told a news conference.

"In a statement (to parliament), RAO Gazprom, RAO United Energy Systems (UES) and the Russian Fuel and Energy Ministry, supported by the government, noted that the 1998 budget should include a separate clause for fuel and energy expenditures by all ministries and departments," Kirikenko said.
"This should also be recommended for local budgets," he added. Without such a clause, enterprises could divert funds from energy payments to wage payments and other needs, he said.

"Even a settling of accounts in existing situations where federal customers owe money to the fuel and energy complex and it owes taxes to the budget is impossible because there is no corresponding separate clause in the budget," Kirikenko said.
Kirinko said that limits on planned energy use would have to be set for each of the federal ministers and departments before the clause could be introduced.
"Under a realistic budget, realistic consumption could be brought in."
Kirinko said that the such a scheme would guarantee normal financing of current payments and normal settling of accounts.
"After this one can start a new stage of work -- bringing the state's existing debts to the fuel and energy complex into a civilised form," Kirienko said.
Since the state is not in a position to pay off its debts immediately, they should be restructured in the form of internal state debt with quite a long repayment period, he said.
"The debts can be restructured in a civilised way. Perhaps seven, perhaps over 10 years, but this must be officially recognised state debt."
The corresponding programmes were being worked on by specialists from the ministries of finance, fuel and energy, Gazprom and UES, he said.
